plans.headline: Treehouses, a train ride and the farmyard

main.why: Your child can climb the Hideaway Woods treehouses, play by the creek, visit the farmyard and ride the train. The Dinosaur Trail is a fun walk too.
tips: Let {them} pick the first stop and follow {their} lead from there.
Bring a snack for a break between the farmyard and the trail.
Tell {them} the train is the last stop, so leaving feels like part of the plan.

source.title: Museum of Life and Science
source.note: Tickets: $24 adults, $19 ages 3–15, under 3 free. Hideaway Woods treehouses and creek, farmyard, train ride and Dinosaur Trail are outside.

alternatives.why: Your child sings and moves along at toddler storytime at Eva Perry Regional Library, then runs off the wiggles at Seagroves Farm Park.
tips: Pick up a ticket at the Youth Services desk when you arrive.
Pack a snack for the park after storytime.

alternatives.why: Your toddler joins the songs and rhymes at Northeast Regional Library, then heads to Plummer Park for the playground.
tips: Sit near the front so {they} can see the books and the movements.
Bring a snack for the playground.

alternatives.why: A quiet morning of nature and playground time. Your child can walk the paths, look for leaves and sticks, and climb on the playground.
tips: Bring a small bucket or bag for treasures along the path.
Pack a snack and eat it at a picnic shelter before you go.

plans.headline: Big outdoor art, wide lawns and trails to explore
